question: A 3-year-old boy is brought to the physician because of recurrent nosebleeds and fatigue for the past 2 months. He also frequently complains his head hurts. The patient has met all motoric milestones for his age but does not like to run because his legs start to hurt if he does. He is at the 40th percentile for both height and weight. His temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F), pulse is 125/min, respirations are 32/min, and blood pressure in the right arm is 130/85 mm Hg. A grade 2/6 systolic murmur is heard in the left paravertebral region. Further evaluation of this patient is most likely to show which of the following findings?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "3-year-old boy with recurrent nosebleeds and fatigue" -> "possible underlying hematologic or vascular issue" -> "elevated blood pressure at 130/85 mm Hg" -> "suggests possible coarctation of the aorta" -> "coarctation can lead to inferior rib notching" -> 85%

CHAIN: "3-year-old boy with recurrent nosebleeds and fatigue" -> "headaches and leg pain during running" -> "possible systemic hypertension" -> "blood pressure discrepancy between upper and lower body" -> "interarm difference in tissue oxygenation may be present" -> 75%

CHAIN: "3-year-old boy with systolic murmur in left paravertebral region" -> "murmur suggests possible vascular abnormality" -> "consideration of coarctation of the aorta" -> "coarctation does not typically cause pulmonary valve stenosis" -> "pulmonary valve stenosis unlikely" -> 70%

CHAIN: "3-year-old boy with elevated blood pressure" -> "possible left ventricular hypertrophy" -> "could lead to left-axis deviation on ECG" -> "but not definitive without further testing" -> "left-axis deviation possible but not certain" -> 65%

CHAIN: "3-year-old boy with leg pain and elevated blood pressure" -> "possible coarctation of the aorta" -> "can lead to delayed pulse in lower extremities" -> "but not confirmed without physical examination" -> "delayed pulse possible but not certain" -> 60%
analysis: The clinical presentation of recurrent nosebleeds, fatigue, headaches, and leg pain with elevated blood pressure in a 3-year-old boy suggests a possible case of coarctation of the aorta. The systolic murmur in the left paravertebral region is indicative of collateral circulation due to the coarctation. Inferior rib notching is a classic finding associated with long-standing coarctation of the aorta due to erosion of the ribs by collateral circulation. Therefore, further evaluation is most likely to show inferior rib notching.
